indicators.note: a down clue would be toppled, but here knocked over tells us the dog's short name is turned backwards

parts.note: a labrador is commonly shortened to lab

explanation.surface: A dog with no fur bumps into someone's daughter and sends her flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bald has no hair on the head, so the word is a plain synonym for being without hair.

parts.note: butter is made from churned cream
someone promoted has moved up

explanation.surface: Margarine looks bland beside a dairy product that has been advertised more heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to compliment them insincerely to win favour, an idiom for flattering.

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the landowner's title is cut out

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish estate owner

explanation.surface: A plump, cruel Highland landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking and baking.

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them hard, as is to pump them for information
kin means one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: An instruction to barbecue a household's big vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grill' looks like cooking, but it means interrogate, which is PUMP; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a large round orange gourd grown and eaten as a vegetable.

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
an usher keeps the door in a court or theatre

explanation.surface: A narcotics seller has a hushed meeting with a porter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pusher is slang for someone who sells illegal drugs, pushing them on users.

clue.text: Maybe part of Sunday's dinner dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a side dish of the traditional British Sunday roast
second meaning: a 1960s novelty dance craze

explanation.walkthrough: A Sunday dinner in Britain is a roast with vegetables, often including this side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato is both a staple of the roast dinner and the name of a popular early-1960s dance.

clue.text: Keep receiving new adverts for protective legwear

indicators.note: receiving means the word keep takes another letter inside it

parts.note: ads is short for adverts

explanation.surface: A shop holds on to fresh advertisements for safety gear worn on the legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneepads are cushioned guards strapped over the knees, worn for protection by skaters and workers.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which is nil

explanation.surface: A Continental romance by a famous waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of north-east Africa, flowing through Egypt.

clue.text: Fraudster once, losing last of medals, ruined cycling event

indicators.note: ruined suggests the remaining letters lie wrecked and are rebuilt in a new order
losing means the named letter is dropped from the phrase before it
last of picks the final letter of medals

explanation.surface: A former cheat stripped of his medals has wrecked a bike race, as happened with doping scandals.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S (last of medals) from FRAUDSTERONCE, then rearrange FRAUDTERONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tour de France is the famous multi-stage annual bicycle race around France.

parts.note: tortoises are proverbially slow animals
hell can mean a state of torment or misery

explanation.surface: Sluggish animals are pestering a blotchy-coated cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoiseshell is a cat whose coat is patched in black, orange and cream, like a tortoise's shell.

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the next three words in turn

explanation.surface: At the end, someone scoffs a pair of chocolate Easter eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to all three words: the last letters of devour, two and chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs carried by a female fish, eaten as food.

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police
to bar something is to stop or block it

explanation.surface: An overzealous police detective sets out to halt a political rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like the rebel being stopped, but it signals turning round the two pieces before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid describes extreme, unreasoning zeal, as in a rabid supporter, borrowing the sense of a mad dog.

indicators.note: heard says the reptile's name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a lizard is a scaly reptile

explanation.surface: Someone hears a British lizard during a spell of bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with high winds, a feature of wintry weather.

clue.text: Beaming artist departs with Tina excitedly

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: excitedly suggests the name Tina being jumbled about in agitation

explanation.surface: A painter leaves happily with his companion Tina, full of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone radiant or beaming is glowing with obvious happiness, a close synonym in the sense of a broad smile.

clue.text: Theft occasionally leading to scrap on square perhaps

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, every other one of theft

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A burglary leads to a brawl in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but is RAG; 'square perhaps' marks the answer as one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragon is any four-sided figure, of which a square is one example.

clue.text: Tender Christian missionary recruiting in force

indicators.note: recruiting means taking in new members, so the apostle's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: St Paul was the great early Christian missionary
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A kindly missionary is out enlisting followers in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: PAUL holds IN plus F, giving PA-INF-UL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender spot is sore to the touch, so tender and painful share the sense of hurting.

clue.text: See double parking? Edward's cut off

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
double says the parking letter appears a second time
P is the road-sign symbol for parking
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward has been caught double parking and his car is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lopped means chopped off, as when branches are trimmed from a tree.

indicators.note: carving reshapes material, so the word stone is cut into a new letter order

explanation.surface: A sculptor begins work on a block of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, as in the onset of winter.

indicators.note: removing the boundaries of a word strips off its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A young person with no limits on behaviour is beyond the pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean not allowed or ruled out, as in 'smoking is out', so it fits unacceptable.

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A buck is glimpsed once more through the morning fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, especially a red deer.

clue.text: Sort of pastry half filled with duck

indicators.note: half takes the opening half of the word filled

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, looking like O

explanation.surface: A kind of pastry half of which is stuffed with duck meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Filo is a paper-thin Greek pastry layered for dishes like baklava.

parts.note: read as the verb schools, meaning trains or teaches
potting is shooting game, as in taking a pot shot

explanation.surface: A school is filming on location for a movie set in the nineties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School's' looks like a possessive noun but is the verb schools, TRAINS; 'shooting' looks like filming but is POTTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainspotting is Danny Boyle's 1996 film about Edinburgh heroin users, based on Irvine Welsh's novel.

clue.text: Dog's den free — a stroke of good luck

indicators.note: free suggests the letters are let loose to settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A kennel that costs nothing is a real piece of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is an unexpected and welcome thing, a blessing that arrives at just the right time.

clue.text: Pairs in middle of slow lane advance

indicators.note: the two central letters of each of the four-letter words are taken, a pair from each

explanation.surface: Couples dawdling down the centre of the slow lane on a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan is money lent, and an advance is a sum paid or lent ahead of time.
